subject: Oncology
content: Oncology is the medical field concerned with the biology, prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and supportive care of cancer.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer is a disease in which abnormal cells grow uncontrollably and may invade nearby tissues or spread to distant sites.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer cells can acquire changes that allow uncontrolled growth, resistance to normal regulatory signals, tissue invasion, and survival in abnormal conditions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Benign tumors do not invade or spread like malignant tumors, whereas malignant tumors can invade surrounding tissues and metastasize.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Metastasis occurs when cancer cells spread from the original tumor to other parts of the body and establish secondary tumors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer risk can be influenced by tobacco, alcohol, infections, ultraviolet and other radiation, environmental exposures, obesity, inherited factors, and age.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer can develop when genetic changes affect genes controlling cell growth, division, DNA repair, and cell survival.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer staging describes the extent of cancer in the body and helps guide prognosis and treatment planning.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Tumor grade describes how abnormal cancer cells look under a microscope and can provide information about tumor behavior.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Tobacco use is a major preventable cause of cancer and is associated with cancers of multiple organs.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Alcohol consumption increases the risk of several cancers, with risk generally increasing as alcohol exposure increases.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Overweight and obesity are associated with increased risk of several cancers and may influence cancer outcomes.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Excessive ultraviolet radiation exposure is a major risk factor for skin cancer, including melanoma and nonmelanoma skin cancers.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer prevention combines reduction of modifiable risk factors, vaccination against cancer-associated infections, appropriate screening, and healthy behaviors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer screening aims to detect disease before symptoms develop and is recommended for selected cancers and populations based on evidence of benefit and harm.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Mammography is an established screening method for breast cancer, with recommendations depending on age, risk, and applicable guidelines.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cervical cancer screening can use HPV testing, cytology, or approved combinations according to age and applicable screening guidance.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Colorectal cancer screening can use stool-based tests, endoscopic tests, or other approved approaches according to risk and screening recommendations.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Low-dose CT can be used to screen selected people at high risk for lung cancer, particularly based on age and smoking history.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer diagnosis generally combines clinical assessment, imaging, laboratory studies, and examination of tissue or cells when appropriate.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: A biopsy removes cells or tissue for examination by a pathologist and is often required to establish a definitive cancer diagnosis.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Pathology evaluates cancer cells and tissue architecture to determine tumor type, grade, and other features important for diagnosis and treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Imaging methods such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, and PET can help detect, characterize, stage, and monitor cancers.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Biomarkers are measurable molecules or characteristics that can provide information about cancer biology, prognosis, or treatment selection.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Molecular tests can identify genetic or other molecular changes in tumors that may help classify cancer or guide targeted treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Leukemia is a cancer of blood-forming tissues characterized by abnormal proliferation of blood cell precursors and is classified into major acute and chronic types.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Lymphoma is cancer arising from lymphocytes and includes Hodgkin lymphoma and several types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell malignancy that can affect bones, blood counts, kidneys, and immune function.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Lung cancer includes several histologic types, with non-small cell and small cell lung cancers representing major categories.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Breast cancer is a group of malignancies arising from breast tissues and is classified by histology and molecular characteristics that influence management.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Colorectal cancer arises in the colon or rectum and may develop from precancerous polyps through accumulation of genetic and cellular changes.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Prostate cancer arises in the prostate gland and has a wide range of biological behavior, from indolent disease to aggressive cancer.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Primary liver cancer includes hepatocellular carcinoma and other malignancies arising in liver tissues.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Pancreatic cancer includes malignancies arising from pancreatic tissues, with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma being the most common type.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Stomach cancer is a malignancy arising in the stomach and includes different histologic and molecular subtypes.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Esophageal cancer includes squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, with risk patterns varying by histologic type and population.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Ovarian cancer includes several tumor types arising from ovarian, fallopian tube, or related tissues and can present at advanced stages.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Endometrial cancer begins in the lining of the uterus and is the most common type of uterine cancer.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Kidney cancer includes several types of renal tumors, with renal cell carcinoma being the most common kidney cancer in adults.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Bladder cancer commonly begins in cells lining the inside of the bladder and may be classified by depth of invasion and histology.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Head and neck cancers arise in structures such as the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, nasal cavity, and related tissues.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Brain and central nervous system tumors can be benign or malignant and are classified by cell type and molecular features.
source: NCI - Brain and Spinal Cord Tumors
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Thyroid cancer includes papillary, follicular, medullary, and anaplastic forms with different biological behavior and treatment approaches.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer treatment may involve surgery, radiation therapy, systemic medicines, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, or combinations selected according to cancer type and stage.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer surgery removes tumors or affected tissues and may be used for diagnosis, local control, cure, palliation, or prevention of complications.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Radiation therapy uses high-energy radiation to damage cancer cells and can be used for curative, adjuvant, or palliative treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Chemotherapy uses drugs that kill cancer cells or inhibit their growth and may be given alone or with other cancer treatments.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Immunotherapy helps the immune system recognize or attack cancer and includes several approaches such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and cellular therapies.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Targeted therapy acts on specific molecules or pathways involved in cancer growth and survival and often depends on the presence of a matching biomarker.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Hormone therapy blocks or lowers hormones that certain cancers require for growth and is used in hormone-sensitive cancers.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Stem cell transplantation can restore blood-forming cells after intensive treatment and is used in selected hematologic cancers and other disorders.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer treatment often combines different modalities to improve tumor control while balancing toxicity and patient-specific factors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer pain can arise from the tumor, treatment, or other causes and should be assessed and managed according to its cause and severity.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer-related fatigue is a common symptom involving persistent tiredness that may not improve adequately with rest and can result from cancer or its treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome involving weight and muscle loss that can occur with advanced cancer and systemic illness.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer and its treatments can cause nausea and vomiting, which may require preventive or therapeutic supportive care.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Neutropenia is a reduction in neutrophils that can increase susceptibility to infection, particularly during some cancer treatments.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Tumor lysis syndrome can occur when large numbers of cancer cells break down rapidly, releasing intracellular contents and causing metabolic abnormalities.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Palliative care focuses on relief of symptoms and treatment-related burdens and can be provided alongside cancer-directed treatment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Hospice provides comfort-focused care for people approaching the end of life and supports patients and families with physical, emotional, and practical needs.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer survivorship includes health and quality-of-life needs during and after cancer treatment, including surveillance and management of late effects.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Some cancer treatments can cause health problems months or years after treatment, requiring long-term follow-up based on prior therapies and cancer history.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Precision medicine uses information about genes, environment, and lifestyle to help prevent or treat disease, including selecting cancer therapies for molecularly defined tumors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Liquid biopsy analyzes tumor-related material such as circulating tumor DNA in blood and may support selected cancer diagnosis, monitoring, or treatment decisions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer clinical trials evaluate new approaches to prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, supportive care, or survivorship.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Oncology
content: Cancer care often involves coordinated input from medical, surgical, radiation, pathology, radiology, nursing, rehabilitation, and supportive-care professionals.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.
